newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian steel workers down tools over BHP closure.
newsitem.headline: Australian steel workers down tools over BHP closure.

text.p: Thousands of Australian steel workers downed tools around the country on Thursday in protest against plans to close the country's oldest steel-making plant.
The 24-hour strike is part of a trade union campaign to reverse a decision by Australia's biggest firm, The Broken Hill Pty Co Ltd (BHP), to shut down the Newcastle steelworks in 1999.
Over 20,000 workers at the 82-year-old Newcastle plant, north of Sydney, and two of BHP's other three steel-making plants walked off the job, causing major disruption.

"Tubemakers and other steel users will also be shut today but I couldn't tell you how many people would be affected," said Maurie Rudd, a spokesman from the steel workers' representative, the Australian Workers Union (AWU).
Rudd said it was possible the strike could continue in some areas on Friday. "They (the workers) may get their tail up a bit and give them a bit more, who knows?," he said.
But BHP said steel production would continue at all its steel-making plants around the country, although the strike would disrupt the chain of supply.

"Parts of the business are customers for other parts of the business and, with a 24-hour continuous operation, it means there's a bit of lag there and a bit of catch-up here," said John Devers, public affairs manager for BHP Steel.
He said it was difficult to gauge the impact on BHP Steel, but the strike could only harm the company's efforts to secure the future of its steel business.
BHP late last month announced the closure of the Newcastle plant, an industrial icon in Australia, because it was inefficient and could not longer match its Asian rivals.
"Strike action is not the answer," Devers told Reuters.
"It's not going to cause the company to change its decision. They are decisions that had to be made to secure the future of our steel businesses throughout Australia."
BHP also denied a radio report that it planned to sell its packaging products operation at its Port Kembla steelworks south of Sydney.
